scope: Product requirements distilled from research; classification is evidence-scoped, not release approval. Candidate notes explicitly distinguish unmerged work; retained follow-ons are in RETAINED-DELIVERY.md.

requirements.statusNote: D-194–D-196 / ADR 0019 accepted; 037 T018–T042 track implementation and actual brief-to-book acceptance.
requirements.statement: Support brief-to-full-book authoring: roughly 100 words of direction and small onboarding lead to autonomous background drafting and revisions toward an author-visible target such as 70,000 saved words.
acceptance: Retain the original brief, onboarding choices, outline and character direction; the approximate brief length is not a hard input cap.
An integrated synthetic journey progresses through plan, chapters, critique, revisions and completion using verified saved-word progress rather than requested/generated token counts.
Pause, restart and failure recovery preserve author edits and durable artifacts without duplicate publication; long-form quality and live-provider outcomes require their own evidence.

requirements.statusNote: Book-owned graph, separate host permission, candidate-only specialists and versioned direction selected; async runtime is not yet implemented.
requirements.statement: Coordinate asynchronous specialist agents in a continuous background authoring workflow with revision cycles, attributable progress and human check-ins for character development and other direction.
acceptance: Accepted contracts define worker ownership, scheduling, context, bounded runtime concurrency and one checked publication path; labels in a single prompt do not establish asynchronous workers.
Check-ins show completed work, next work and specific questions; answers update versioned direction and dependent work respects unresolved questions.
Stop/revoke, spend limits, unavailable providers, hidden-window and quit/restart behavior have truthful durable states and failure tests before unattended execution is claimed.

requirements.statusNote: D-197–D-199 / ADR 0020 accepted; exact-current CodeMirror adapter, explicit saved feedback and campaign implementation remain.
requirements.statement: Provide AutoCrit-style editorial critique with underlined source passages, linked explanations and navigable/filterable feedback, while distinguishing deterministic metrics from subjective interpretation.
acceptance: Underlines and finding selection resolve to exact saved-source spans, with keyboard access and clear handling of overlaps and repeated passages.
Edits, missing sources and changed revisions make feedback stale rather than silently attaching it to different words.
Any suggestion-application flow uses checked edits and undo; product-comparison research is not a claim of feature or score parity.

requirements.statusNote: D-200 / ADR 0021 accepted; pure sessions precede host and acoustic qualification. 038 T022 remains unchecked.
requirements.statement: Support a hands-free authoring journey with spoken direction, replies and check-ins, interruption/stop and correction, beyond existing push-to-talk transcription.
acceptance: An accepted activation/listening contract states visible and audible capture/work states and when microphone use begins and ends.
Synthetic interaction tests cover interruption, stop, confirmation, misrecognition, provider failure and an accessible non-voice fallback.
Live microphone, provider and device evidence is recorded separately; existing voice preferences or spoken replies alone do not complete this journey.

requirements.statement: Keep one studio-owned tool catalog across the built-in agent, loopback backend, CLI, and MCP; preserve checked writes, explicit write/destructive opt-ins, and the desktop library as the only writer.
acceptance: A parity test compares the studio catalog with backend and MCP discovery.
Writes require explicit opt-in; destructive calls require the separate destructive opt-in and remain undoable.
The toolkit cannot open a second library or access provider credentials.

requirements.statement: Keep deterministic reports local, explicit, read-only, and grounded in saved-source revisions; state coverage and stale evidence honestly.
acceptance: Synthetic fixtures prove saved-only input, shared word-count semantics, cancellation, stale detection, and byte-identical library files.
The report distinguishes complete, partial, stopped, stale, and insufficient-evidence outcomes.
D-198 repetition v1 preserves every exact occurrence; D-199 explicit retention requires detailed formats and recoverable writes. Neither decision alone establishes implementation.

requirements.statement: Keep conversational model review separate from structured reports; disclose provider, model, and exact selected source scope before sending, cite verified revisions, and never edit or silently widen scope.
acceptance: A cancel before the explicit provider-named start produces zero provider requests.
Only selected source content is sent; each source-backed observation resolves to the captured revision.
Write, destructive, disabled, and plugin tools are unavailable to the read-only review.

requirements.statement: Treat structured critique, reader profiles and rereads, and cross-book analysis as explicitly scoped additions with consent, evidence, retention, and no-write rules.
acceptance: A structured finding is schema-validated and its quotation is verified against the supplied source.
Reader identity and prior feedback are attributed to the correct run and are not silently relabelled or overwritten.
Series findings identify every included book and distinguish manuscript evidence from outline or note evidence.
No report history is persisted before the applicable retention decision is accepted.

requirements.statement: Distinguish press-to-talk transcription, spoken replies/read-aloud, and any future continuous conversation; do not imply always-on listening or barge-in without a separate verified contract.
acceptance: The interface identifies when recording starts and stops and makes the recognized text visible.
Voice-service failure has a truthful fallback or refusal and does not silently lose the author's request.

Persistent preferences use integrated spec 038 and D-192: explicit catalog-validated selections, no Settings probes and no silent provider switching. T022 remains open; automated evidence does not establish live-provider acceptance.

requirements.statement: Export from a saved immutable snapshot, preserve source files, and label approximate previews and unsupported targets truthfully.
acceptance: A failure-injected export leaves the source and prior destination intact.
Markdown folder export is tested as an ordinary folder in book order, including ordered matter.
The UI does not imply measured pagination, print compatibility, or publisher acceptance.

requirements.statement: Claim publishing readiness only for a named target and rule-set version after measurable validation; report actionable errors and unknowns without uploading the manuscript.
acceptance: Print and eBook checks are separate and identify the rule-set version and measured inputs.
Unknown measurements produce an unknown result, not a passing status.
A readiness claim is unavailable unless every required target-specific check passes.

requirements.statement: Define Android as its own supported target with tested storage, file-picker, credential, import/export, and lifecycle capability gates; do not infer support from iOS or browser behavior.
acceptance: A target matrix names supported Android versions and each available capability.
Storage, credential, picker, save/conflict, and app lifecycle tests pass on the approved Android target.
Unsupported import, export, sync, or provider actions are refused before data is captured or written.

requirements.statement: Specify book-level cover composition and output as a distinct capability from chapter illustrations; preserve source assets and validate target-specific dimensions before claiming readiness.
acceptance: Cover assets and layout are book-level and do not alter chapter illustration attachments.
The author can preview and export a cover without modifying the manuscript or source assets.
A cover/spine result names its target, required dimensions, inputs, and any unknowns.

requirements.statement: Define narrator and optional character casting, pronunciation/editing controls, per-chapter generation, audio packaging, and disclosure/consent before sending manuscript text to a voice provider.
acceptance: The author reviews the selected text, provider, voices, and output before generation begins.
Generated audio is traceable to a saved book snapshot and does not modify manuscript files.
A failed or cancelled chapter does not publish a partial audiobook as complete; successful chapters remain recoverable.
No voice cloning or third-party voice imitation is implied by narrator or character casting.

requirements.statement: Add collections, recent work, goals, or source-anchored notes only through existing library/file and conflict contracts, with explicit retention and scope.
acceptance: A synthetic multi-book library preserves book identity, search, counts, and recoverable trash behavior.
Collection and note updates survive reload without dropping unknown book fields or losing conflicting edits.
Recent-work and goal failures are not presented as successful updates.

requirements.statusNote: Verified saved-only core merged in PR33. Restore/UI correction56c7b7d passed exact-head broad gates, was accepted by fresh independent review and merged in PR34; host mounting remains. Original candidates are preserved.
requirements.statement: Add named snapshots and restore only after storage, retention, conflict, and undo semantics are accepted; preserve both current and restored text.
acceptance: History storage and retention decisions are accepted before persistence tasks begin.
A restore against a changed source preserves the current text and reports the conflict instead of overwriting it.
Restore is attributable and has a tested undo/recovery path.

requirements.statusNote: Offline preview leaf exists but is unmounted. D-196 selects explicit pinned workflow routes; D-116 selects bounded-operation versus qualified strict-money mode. Enforcement/adapter qualification remain.
requirements.statement: Keep task-aware routing advisory until policy is accepted; preserve author-selected dispatch, actual-model attribution, and unknown cost, and do not infer a budget ceiling.
acceptance: Opening or changing the preview causes zero provider calls, credential reads, catalog refreshes, or library writes.
Unknown capability, context, and price facts remain unknown and are not converted to a rank or zero cost.
No automatic dispatch, fallback, retry, or enforceable ceiling ships without its own accepted public decision.

requirements.statement: Keep release signing and update claims behind their decisions; identify artifact provenance and unsigned status, and never let an app update modify the author library.
acceptance: Unsigned builds are labelled for informed testing and are not represented as signed public releases.
Signing, notarization, and update-feed work starts only after D-115 is accepted.
Any approved install/update test proves library and app-profile preservation and refuses incompatible schema safely.

requirements.statement: State capability by product surface and platform; do not infer browser, mobile, glasses, or Android support from desktop behavior.
acceptance: A surface-by-capability matrix is reflected in the UI and release record.
A refused capability has a specific explanation and does not begin a recording, provider request, or partial file operation.
